causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Demand in New South Wales reached 12 333 MW, which was 800 MW higher than forecast four hours ahead and 350 MW higher than forecast at the beginning of the trading interval.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Liddell unit 4 513 Unit tripped on 2 January and remained out of service on this day.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Munmorah unit 4 300 Shutdown on 11 December, returned to service on 27 January. Vales Point unit 6 660 Shutdown on 15 December, returned to service on 14 January.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: In New South Wales 1490 MW (or 14 per cent) of capacity was priced above $5000/MWh. Of this capacity, up to 870 MW resulted from rebidding by Macquarie Generation from relatively low prices during the day.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: An unplanned transmission outage caused a significant step reduction in imports from Queensland into New South Wales at around 3.45 pm, increasing prices in New South Wales.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: At 3.45 pm, a combined reduction of more than 600 MW in import capability across the Queensland to New South Wales interconnectors occurred.

constraints_named.quote: The rebid reason given was "Manage Snowy CSC/CSP constraints".
The rebid reason given was "Manage unexp Snowy- NSW constraint Band up".
The rebid reason given was "Manage unexp Snow-Vic constraint bnd up".

interconnectors_named.name: Queensland to New South Wales interconnectors
interconnectors_named.quote: At 3.45 pm, a combined reduction of more than 600 MW in import capability across the Queensland to New South Wales interconnectors occurred.

interconnectors_named.name: Snowy and Queensland interconnectors
interconnectors_named.quote: Flows across the Snowy and Queensland interconnectors were unconstrained for all but one dispatch interval during the trading interval.

intervals.quote: During the 4.00 pm trading interval (which covers the half hour from 3.30 pm to 4.00 pm) five minute dispatch prices were aligned with Victoria and Queensland at less than $600/MWh until 3.45 pm, when the transmission outage occurred.
intervals.text: the 4 pm trading interval (which covers the half hour from 3.30 pm to 4.00 pm)

network_outages.quote: An unplanned transmission outage caused a significant step reduction in imports from Queensland into New South Wales at around 3.45 pm, increasing prices in New South Wales.

peak_price.quote: This saw step changes in prices from $527/MWh in New South Wales and $506/MWh in Queensland at 3.40 pm to $9350/MWh in New South Wales and $81/MWh in Queensland at 3.45 pm.

rebid_set_price.quote: a rebid into higher prices by Snowy Hydro, saw the prices across the regions realign at more than $4800/MWh for the remainder of the trading interval.
